{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABf4F3nQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhJVjpI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 142, "title": "Add optional CRT-style shader rendering with Pixel/CRT comparison", "body": "## Problem

The browser frontend currently displays the raw Rust/Wasm framebuffer with Canvas 2D `putImageData`, then scales it via `image-rendering: pixelated`. This is a useful crisp baseline, but it does not resemble the softer image from a period CRT television. The maintainer would like an optional **CRT-style post-processing shader** so visitors can compare the original pixels with a convincing, restrained retro-TV presentation.

Baseline inspected at `main` `096b46bc72a0d0d6fe92cd90707e4ad0650583f2`:
- [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js) gets a Canvas 2D context, creates an `ImageData`, and writes the core framebuffer via `putImageData()`. The framebuffer can change between low-res (256-pixel) and hi-res (512-pixel) modes.
- [`web/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css) enlarges the canvas with `image-rendering: pixelated`; portrait and short-landscape touch layouts are tightly space-constrained.
- [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html) already has a `Help / Controls` disclosure containing the Scale setting.

## Expected outcome

Introduce a small **Display: Pixel | CRT** choice for the browser emulator:
- **Pixel**: today's unmodified, crisp pixel output (a stable reference view).
- **CRT**: a tastefully restrained shader approximating a **consumer CRT television**, using subtle scanlines, mild horizontal color blending/softness, restrained glow and (only if visually useful) a low-strength phosphor/aperture texture.
- Switching between Pixel and CRT should be instant and **must not restart or pause the game**, change cartridge state, change audio, or affect controller input. Visitors can compare **the same live game scene** in each mode. Persist their selection as a browser preference where available; default to **Pixel** for current-user compatibility until they explicitly choose CRT.

Treat this as a **visual interpretation**, not a verified hardware-accurate reconstruction of an NTSC composite/RGB signal. Do not claim exact physical colorimetry or emulate composite artifacts unless explicitly implemented and validated. Avoid exaggerated curvature, thick black scanlines, flicker, grain and large decorative TV bezels by default; readability of dialogue and UI in both bundled demos matters more than spectacle.

## Design and technical scope

- Implement the CRT processing as **browser-side GPU post-processing**, e.g. a compact WebGL fragment shader. The Rust/Wasm emulator, its framebuffer bytes, CPU/PPU and gameplay must remain unchanged. Keep the original crisp path as a real working fallback. A WebGL context cannot be simultaneously acquired as Canvas 2D from the same element: explicitly design a safe source framebuffer -> display pipeline (offscreen/staging or separate presentation surface) rather than attempting incompatible contexts on one canvas.
- Choose a clear shader input/output color convention; preserve alpha/opacity and avoid clipping, aggressive blur or dimming. Scanline spacing should derive from the **emulated source resolution**, not raw device pixels. Make the effect robust across 256×224, 512-wide hires and any supported framebuffer dimension/resizing/fullscreen. Avoid shimmering/moire when scaled down on mobile/retina screens; reduce or omit fine-grained mask/scanlines at insufficient display resolution.
- **GPU failure handling is required**: if WebGL is unavailable, shader compilation/linking fails, context is lost, or performance is insufficient, continue showing playable frames using the existing Pixel renderer and show a brief, unobtrusive recoverable indication if useful. Do not leave a black canvas, crash emulation, or trap the user on a broken CRT mode. Avoid adding a large shader library or heavyweight dependency for this small effect.
- Keep a simple, unobtrusive **Display** selector, preferably next to the existing Scale setting under Help / Controls. Do not add a permanent large panel, duplicate control, retro-TV cabinet art or prose-heavy walkthrough; adhere to [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable**. Make it keyboard/touch/screen-reader accessible with an accurate selected state. Preserve existing canvas focus/input behavior.
- Keep video geometry, 256/512-pixel output, aspect ratio, image edge behavior, placeholder visibility, paused frame, screenshots/display capture where supported, scaling, fullscreen, and overlay ordering intact. The renderer should not corrupt the display after cartridge reset, ROM switching, tab visibility changes, GPU recovery, or resize.
- Provide a simple reproducible visual comparison in the PR: **same-scene Pixel versus CRT screenshots for both bundled games** (潮鳴りの密室 and 夜鳴き鐘), preferably with a short note about why the selected intensity retains text readability. Screenshot capture must use the actual running browser renderer, **not concept images**. A small RGB-like crisp CRT variant can be discussed later; keep the initial task to **one conservative CRT mode plus Pixel**, unless adding an alternate preset clearly avoids complexity.
- Keep emulation responsive on desktop **and** midrange mobile hardware. Target the existing frame pacing, avoid unnecessary CPU pixel transformations/allocations on each frame, limit texture copies/postprocessing passes, and measure before/after rendering overhead. Do not claim performance improvement without measurements; do not gate on an invented benchmark threshold.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] The app offers an accessible, compact **Pixel / CRT** display selection and switching does not interrupt real Wasm gameplay, frames, input, audio or SRAM. It is easy to compare the same live scene. Preference persistence is best-effort and robust against missing/corrupt browser storage.
- [ ] Pixel mode matches the current observable output (including crisp edges), with correct low-res and hires geometry. No regression in reset-to-playing, cartridge switching, two bundled demo ROMs or local file play.
- [ ] CRT mode visibly demonstrates a **subtle CRT look** (scanlines and modest color softness/glow) while the text and imagery of both original Japanese demos remain readable. Do not make screens substantially darker or distort geometry. Validate both 256 and 512 source widths, non-integer scale, resizing and fullscreen.
- [ ] Actual browser screenshots compare Pixel and CRT **for the same frame/scene** from 潮鳴りの密室 and 夜鳴き鐘, preferably also a hires test fixture. Preserve documentation of chosen effect strength and limits; do not present a reference photo as a screenshot of the implementation.
- [ ] Test WebGL shader initialization, live frame updates, mode switching, window resizing, context loss/restore (where automatable), unsupported WebGL/failure fallback, clean exit from CRT mode and no black screen. No uncaught errors, CSP issues, GPU resource leaks, or accessibility/focus regressions.
- [ ] Desktop, portrait and short-height landscape viewports retain the **same screen-first layout**, visible 12-button SNES touch controls, safe-area handling, keyboard/gamepad/multitouch, accessible picker and compact toolbar with always-visible volume/mute slider; shader choices do not occlude video or touch controls.
- [ ] Measure representative Pixel and CRT frame times or workload overhead on the development machine/browser and, where feasible, a resource-constrained configuration; record the method, figures and any skips, ensuring no obvious dropped-frame regression or runaway GPU/CPU work. Pixel fallback remains usable on limited devices.
- [ ] Run the repository's applicable format/lint/unit, production Wasm/static build, required browser/Pages tests and source-built game/hardware validation gates appropriate to the actual diff. Preserve existing published file allowlist and pinned demo hashes/legal notices; report the checks actually executed and any exceptions. Update minimal README/Help copy without overexplaining the feature.

## Optional validation

Physical iOS Safari / Android Chrome (including low-power phones), real CRT/TV photographic comparison, GPU profiling and accessibility review. These may inform follow-ups; do not require physical hardware when required automated tests pass.

## Post-merge verification

After the PR merges, check the new `main` GitHub Pages deployment and the actual published app with both Pixel and CRT across desktop/mobile viewports, inspecting text readability, frame updates, failure behavior, CSP and console errors. Record the real run and URL/results. This occurs **after merge**, not as a pre-merge gate; create a separate `task` Issue with evidence if anything fails when invoked. No implied background monitoring.

## Related work

- [Issue #116](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/116): responsive SNES touch controls.
- [Issue #118](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/118): emulator-first visual hierarchy.
- [Issue #122](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/122): persistent cartridge slot and unified selection.
- [Issue #134](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/134): volume and mute toolbar.
